questions.question: Which of the following is a common category of agents that can cause diseases in poultry fowl?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Viruses, bacteria, and fungi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poultry fowl** are susceptible to various diseases caused by different types of infectious agents, primarily **viruses**, **bacteria**, and **fungi**.
 
• **Viruses** are responsible for some of the most devastating poultry diseases. For example, **Ranikhet disease** (also known as **Newcastle Disease**) and **Avian Influenza** (commonly called **Bird Flu**) are highly contagious viral infections that can lead to mass mortality in flocks. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Bacteria** cause several serious conditions such as **Fowl Cholera**, **Salmonellosis** (including **Pullorum disease**), and **Chronic Respiratory Disease (CRD)**. These bacterial infections often lead to reduced egg production and growth rates.
 
• **Fungi** can cause diseases like **Aspergillosis** (Brooder pneumonia), which typically occurs when birds inhale spores from moldy **litter** or **contaminated feed**. Fungal toxins, known as **mycotoxins**, can also severely impact poultry health.
 
• While **purely genetic factors** can lead to certain hereditary abnormalities or predispositions, they are not categorized as the common external "agents" that cause infectious disease outbreaks in poultry. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Vitamins and minerals** are essential nutrients; their deficiency causes **nutritional deficiency diseases** (like **Rickets** due to lack of **Vitamin D**), but they are not causative agents of infectious diseases. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sunlight exposure** is generally beneficial for poultry as it helps in the synthesis of **Vitamin D3** and acts as a natural disinfectant, rather than being a disease-causing agent. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biosecurity Measures**: 
 
 
• To prevent the spread of **viruses** and **bacteria**, poultry farms must implement strict **biosecurity** protocols. This includes regular **cleaning** and **disinfection** of poultry sheds.
 
• Restricting the entry of unauthorized persons and managing the movement of **equipment** helps minimize the risk of pathogen introduction.
 
 
 
• **Vaccination Programs**:
 
 
• **Vaccination** is a critical management practice used to provide **immunity** against viral diseases like **Newcastle Disease** and **Infectious Bursal Disease (Gumboro)**.
 
• Vaccines are usually administered through **drinking water**, **eye drops**, or **injections** at specific **ages** (e.g., **Day 1**, **Week 1**, etc.).
 
 
 
• **Parasitic Infestations**:
 
 
• Apart from microorganisms, poultry are also affected by **parasites**. **Internal parasites** include **roundworms** and **tapeworms**, while **external parasites** include **mites**, **ticks**, and **lice**.
 
• **Coccidiosis** is a significant disease caused by **protozoa** that affects the intestinal tract of the birds, leading to **bloody diarrhea**.
 
 
 
• **Management Practices**:
 
 
• Proper **ventilation**, **temperature control**, and **waste management** are essential to keep the birds healthy and reduce the load of **fungal spores** and **ammonia** gas in the environment.
 
• **Quality feed** and **clean water** are fundamental to maintaining the **immune system** of the fowl, helping them resist common infections.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following situations demonstrates Newton’s Second Law of Motion?

options.text: A car speeding up on the road
A man standing inside a lift
A book lying still on the table

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A car speeding up on the road**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Second Law of Motion** states that the **acceleration** of an object as produced by a **net force** is directly proportional to the magnitude of the net force, in the same direction as the net force, and inversely proportional to the **mass** of the object.
 
• This law is mathematically expressed as **F = ma**, where **F** is the force applied, **m** is the mass, and **a** is the acceleration produced.
 
• In the situation of **a car speeding up on the road**, the engine generates a **net force** that acts on the car's **mass**. Because this force is **unbalanced**, the car undergoes a change in **velocity** over **time**, which is defined as **acceleration**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• A **man standing inside a lift** (assuming the lift is stationary or moving at a **constant velocity**) demonstrates a state of **equilibrium**. Here, the **downward gravitational force** is perfectly balanced by the **upward normal force** from the floor, resulting in zero net force and zero acceleration. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect in the context of demonstrating a net force causing acceleration.***
 
• A **book lying still on the table** is a classic example of **Newton’s First Law of Motion** (the **Law of Inertia**). The object remains at **rest** because the net external force acting on it is **zero**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• While a **satellite moving around Earth** does involve the Second Law (as **gravity** acts as a **centripetal force** causing **centripetal acceleration** by changing the satellite's direction), the most direct and common textbook demonstration of a change in **magnitude of velocity** (speeding up) due to an applied force is the accelerating car.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s First Law of Motion**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will not change its motion unless acted upon by an **unbalanced force**.
 
• If the object is at **rest**, it stays at rest. If it is in **motion**, it remains in motion at the same **speed** and in a straight line.
 
• **Inertia** is the tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion; it is directly related to the **mass** of the object.
 
 
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**:
 
 
• This law states that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**.
 
• Forces always exist in **pairs**. When object A exerts a force on object B, object B simultaneously exerts a force of equal magnitude and opposite direction on object A.
 
• Examples include **recoil of a gun**, **swimming**, or a **rocket launch**.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Momentum**:
 
 
• Newton's Second Law is also defined as the **rate of change of momentum**.
 
• **Momentum (p)** is the product of **mass (m)** and **velocity (v)**. The law states that **Force** is proportional to the **change in momentum** divided by **time (t)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sir Isaac Newton**: He first formulated these three laws of motion in his monumental work titled **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"**, published in the year **1687**.
 
• **SI Unit of Force**: The standard unit of force is the **Newton (N)**. One Newton is defined as the amount of force required to accelerate a **1 kilogram** mass at a rate of **1 meter per second squared (1 m/s²)**.
 
• **Vector Nature**: Both **Force** and **Acceleration** are **vector quantities**, meaning they have both **magnitude** and **direction**. The acceleration of the car happens in the same direction as the net force applied by the wheels against the road.
 
• **Mass vs. Weight**: **Mass** is an intrinsic property representing the amount of matter (measured in **kg**), while **Weight** is the **force of gravity** acting on that mass (measured in **Newtons**), calculated as **W = mg**, where **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth.

questions.question:
Select the correct option regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to form calcium hydroxide.
Reason (R): In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form one product.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that **calcium oxide** reacts vigorously with **water** to produce **calcium hydroxide** (slaked lime). This observation is scientifically accurate as the reaction is highly **exothermic**, releasing a significant amount of heat energy. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** defines a **combination reaction** as a process where two or more reactants (elements or compounds) fuse to form a **single product**. ***Hence, statement R is correct.***
 
• In the chemical reaction mentioned, **CaO (Calcium oxide)** and **H2O (Water)** are the two reactants that combine to form one single product, **Ca(OH)2 (Calcium hydroxide)**.
 
• Since the reaction described in the assertion is a classic example of the definition provided in the reason, the reason serves as the correct theoretical explanation for the classification and nature of the assertion. ***Hence, R is the correct explanation of A.***
 
• The chemical equation representing this reaction is: **CaO (s) + H2O (l) → Ca(OH)2 (aq) + Heat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium Oxide (CaO):**
 
 
• Commonly known as **quicklime** or **burnt lime**, it is a white, caustic, and alkaline crystalline solid.
 
• It is widely used in **industry** for making **steel**, **paper**, and in **water treatment** processes.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2):**
 
 
• Commonly referred to as **slaked lime**. A dilute solution of calcium hydroxide is known as **lime water**.
 
• It is used for **whitewashing** walls. After application, it reacts with **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** in the air to form a thin, shiny layer of **calcium carbonate (CaCO3)** over **two to three days**.
 
 
 
• **Exothermic Reactions:**
 
 
• These are chemical reactions that release energy in the form of **light or heat**.
 
• The reaction between **quicklime and water** is so energetic that it can cause the water to reach its **boiling point**, producing a hissing sound.
 
• Another common example of an exothermic combination reaction is the **burning of coal** (Carbon + Oxygen → Carbon Dioxide).
 
 
 
• **Types of Chemical Reactions:**
 
 
• **Decomposition Reaction:** A single reactant breaks down to give simpler products (the opposite of combination).
 
• **Displacement Reaction:** A more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• **Double Displacement:** An exchange of ions between the reactants occurs to form new compounds, often resulting in a **precipitate**.

questions.question: Sodium hydroxide is formed by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Passing electricity through brine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sodium hydroxide** (NaOH) is produced on an industrial scale through a specific method called the **Chlor-alkali process**.
 
• This process involves the **electrolysis** of an aqueous solution of **sodium chloride**, which is commonly referred to as **brine**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• When **electricity** is passed through **brine**, the **sodium chloride** decomposes to form **sodium hydroxide**, **chlorine gas**, and **hydrogen gas**.
 
• The overall chemical reaction for this process is: **2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl2(g) + H2(g)**.
 
• During this electrolytic reaction, **chlorine gas** is given off at the **anode** (the positive electrode), while **hydrogen gas** is released at the **cathode** (the negative electrode).
 
• The **sodium hydroxide solution** is formed specifically near the **cathode**, where it is collected for further use.

questions.question: In the case of a convex lens, under what specific object position is the image formed at 2F (F is the focal length) and has the same size as the object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**At 2F**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed at **2F** (also known as the **Center of Curvature**, **C**) of a **convex lens**, the rays of light from the object converge on the opposite side of the lens at exactly the **2F** position.
 
• In this specific configuration, the **object distance (u)** is equal to **2f**, and the **image distance (v)** is also **2f**. ***Hence, the statement in the question is correct.***
 
• The image formed at **2F** has the unique characteristic of being **exactly the same size** as the object. The **linear magnification (m)** in this case is **-1**, where the negative sign indicates the image is **inverted**.
 
• The nature of the image formed is **real** and **inverted**. A **real image** is one where the light rays actually meet at a point, allowing the image to be projected onto a **screen**.
 
• For a **convex lens**, which is a **converging lens**, this is the only position (other than infinity for a point image) where the distance of the object from the lens equals the distance of the image from the lens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Object at Infinity:**
 
 
• When the object is at an **infinite distance**, the incident rays are parallel to the **principal axis**.
 
• The image is formed at the **Principal Focus (F)** on the other side.
 
• The image is **highly diminished** (point-sized), **real**, and **inverted**.
 
 
 
• **Object Beyond 2F:**
 
 
• When the object is placed at a distance greater than **twice the focal length**, the image is formed between **F** and **2F** on the opposite side.
 
• The image is **diminished** (smaller than the object), **real**, and **inverted**.
 
 
 
• **Object at Focus (F):**
 
 
• When the object is placed exactly at the **Focus (F)**, the refracted rays emerge parallel to each other.
 
• The image is formed at **infinity**.
 
• The image is **highly magnified**, **real**, and **inverted**.
 
 
 
• **Object Between F and Optical Center (O):**
 
 
• This is the only case for a **convex lens** where a **virtual image** is formed.
 
• The image is formed on the **same side** as the object, and it is **enlarged** and **erect**. This principle is used in a **magnifying glass**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula:** The relationship between the **focal length (f)**, **object distance (u)**, and **image distance (v)** is given by the formula: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the **object distance (u)** is always **negative**. For a **convex lens**, the **focal length (f)** is always **positive**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** It is defined as the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**, or **m = v/u**. In the case where the object is at **2F**, **v = 2f** and **u = -2f**, leading to **m = -1**.
 
• **Applications:** Convex lenses are widely used in **spectacles** to correct **Hypermetropia** (farsightedness), in **cameras** to focus light on film or sensors, and in **microscopes** and **telescopes** to magnify distant or tiny objects.
 
• **Focal Length (F):** The distance from the **optical center** to the **principal focus**. It depends on the **refractive index** of the lens material and the **radii of curvature** of its surfaces.
</ul

questions.question: The total resistance of 5 resistors of equal resistance R arranged in a parallel arrangement is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R/5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **parallel arrangement** of resistors, the **reciprocal of the equivalent resistance** is equal to the **sum of the reciprocals** of the individual resistances.
 
• The mathematical formula for the **total resistance (Rp)** in a parallel circuit is given by: **1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3 + ... + 1/Rn**.
 
• When **5 resistors** of **equal resistance R** are connected in parallel, the equation becomes: **1/Rp = 1/R + 1/R + 1/R + 1/R + 1/R**.
 
• By adding the fractions, we get **1/Rp = 5/R**. To find the value of the total resistance, we take the **reciprocal** of both sides, which results in **Rp = R/5**.
 
• This principle demonstrates that in a parallel circuit, the **equivalent resistance** is always **smaller** than the smallest individual resistance in the network.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Series Combination**: In a **series arrangement**, the resistors are connected end-to-end. The **total resistance (Rs)** is the simple **arithmetic sum** of the individual resistances: **Rs = R1 + R2 + ... + Rn**. For **5 resistors** of value **R** in series, the total resistance would be **5R**.
 
• **Voltage and Current**: In a **parallel circuit**, the **potential difference (Voltage)** across each resistor remains **constant** and equal to the source voltage. However, the **total current** from the source is **distributed** among the different parallel branches.
 
• **Applications**: **Domestic household wiring** is typically done in **parallel**. This ensures that even if one appliance (resistor) fails or is turned off, the **circuit remains closed** for other appliances, and all devices receive the **rated voltage** (e.g., **220V** in India).
 
• **Ohm's Law**: The fundamental relationship used to analyze these circuits is **Ohm's Law**, which states **V = IR**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• For **n equal resistors** each of resistance **R**, the **equivalent resistance in parallel** is always **R/n**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **electrical resistance** is the **Ohm**, symbolized by the Greek letter **Ω (Omega)**.
 
• Conductance is the **reciprocal of resistance**; therefore, in a parallel circuit, the **total conductance** is the sum of the individual conductances of the branches.
 
• When comparing the two types of connections for **n identical resistors**, the ratio of **Series Resistance (Rs)** to **Parallel Resistance (Rp)** is always **n²**. In this specific case with **5 resistors**, the ratio **Rs/Rp** would be **25**.

questions.question: Which of the following phenomena CANNOT be explained without dispersion of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rainbow formation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rainbow formation** is a natural phenomenon that involves a combination of **dispersion**, **refraction**, and **internal reflection** of sunlight by spherical water droplets in the atmosphere. Without **dispersion**, the light would not split into its **seven constituent colors** (**VIBGYOR**), and the rainbow would not be visible in its colored form. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Twinkling of stars** is primarily caused by **atmospheric refraction**. As starlight enters the Earth's atmosphere, it undergoes multiple refractions due to varying **optical densities** and temperatures of air layers, causing the apparent position and brightness of the star to fluctuate. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Advanced sunrise** and delayed sunset occur because of **atmospheric refraction**. The Sun is visible to us about **2 minutes** before the actual sunrise because light bends as it travels from the vacuum of space into the denser Earth's atmosphere. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Mirages** are optical illusions typically observed in hot deserts or on coal-tar roads during **summer**. They are caused by **Total Internal Reflection (TIR)** and **refraction** as light passes through layers of air with different **temperature gradients**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Dispersion of light** is defined as the splitting of a beam of **white light** into its individual spectrum of colors when it passes through a transparent medium like a **glass prism** or water droplet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dispersion of Light:**
 
 
• This phenomenon was first discovered by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1666**.
 
• In the visible spectrum, **Red light** has the **longest wavelength** and deviates the least, while **Violet light** has the **shortest wavelength** and deviates the most.
 
• The band of colored components of a light beam is called its **spectrum**, commonly represented by the acronym **VIBGYOR** (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction:**
 
 
• The Earth's atmosphere is not uniform; its **refractive index** changes with altitude and temperature.
 
• Besides twinkling and advanced sunrise, this also causes the **flattening of the Sun's disc** at sunrise and sunset.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection (TIR):**
 
 
• It occurs when light travels from a **denser medium** to a **rarer medium** and the **angle of incidence** is greater than the **critical angle**.
 
• **TIR** is the principle behind the working of **optical fibers** and the **brilliance of diamonds**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Condition for Rainbow:** A rainbow is always formed in a direction **opposite** to that of the Sun. The water droplets act like small **prisms**.
 
• **Primary vs Secondary Rainbow:** A **primary rainbow** involves **two refractions** and **one internal reflection**, whereas a **secondary rainbow** involves **two internal reflections**, resulting in reversed colors.
 
• **Refraction:** It is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another due to the change in the **velocity of light**. The degree of bending depends on the **refractive index** of the media involved.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following contributes directly to forest conservation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Social Forestry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Social Forestry** involves the management and protection of forests as well as **afforestation** on barren lands with the purpose of helping in the environmental, social, and rural development of the country. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It aims at increasing forest cover to reduce the pressure on traditional forest areas by growing trees on community lands, canal banks, and railway lines. This directly contributes to **forest conservation** by providing alternative sources of **fuelwood** and **timber**.
 
• **Mining** involves the extraction of minerals from the earth's crust. It is a major cause of **deforestation** and land degradation because it requires clearing vast areas of forest land for excavation and infrastructure. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Urbanization** is the process of the expansion of cities and the migration of people from rural to urban areas. This leads to the conversion of forest land into residential and industrial zones, causing a net loss in **biodiversity**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Logging** refers to the activity of cutting down trees for commercial timber or fuel. While it can be managed, it is traditionally an extractive industry that leads to **forest thinning** and habitat loss rather than conservation. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of Social Forestry:** The term was first used in **India** in **1976** by the **National Commission on Agriculture**. It was launched to encourage people to plant trees on their own land and common lands to meet the needs of the rural population.
 
• **Components:** Social forestry is broadly categorized into **Farm Forestry**, **Community Forestry**, **Extension Forestry**, and **Agro-forestry**.
 
 
• **Farm Forestry**: Farmers grow trees for commercial or non-commercial purposes on their own **agricultural lands**.
 
• **Community Forestry**: The **community** as a whole takes the initiative to plant trees on public or community-owned lands.
 
 
 
• **Objectives:** The primary goals include providing **fodder** for livestock, **fuelwood** for cooking, and **small timber** for rural housing, thereby preventing the local population from exploiting **Reserved Forests**.
 
• **Policy Framework:** The **National Forest Policy of 1988** emphasized the need for a massive people's movement for afforestation and advocated that the forest-based industry should encourage small-scale farmers to grow raw materials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Benefits:** Social forestry helps in **carbon sequestration**, which is vital for mitigating **climate change**. It also helps in **soil conservation** by preventing wind and water erosion in rural tracts.
 
• **Target Goal:** India aims to bring **33%** of its total geographical area under forest and tree cover, a target highlighted in the **National Forest Policy**.
 
• **Role of International Organizations:** During the **1980s**, several Social Forestry projects in India were funded by international agencies like the **World Bank** and the **United States Agency for International Development (USAID)** to promote **sustainable land management**.
 
• **Employment:** These programs generate significant **employment** opportunities for the rural poor, particularly through tree planting, nursery management, and the harvesting of **non-timber forest products (NTFP)**.
</ul

questions.question: In galvanisation, which metal is used to coat iron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanisation** is a chemical process used to prevent the **rusting** of **iron** and **steel** by applying a protective **zinc** coating.
 
• The process primarily utilizes **zinc** because it is more **reactive** than iron and acts as a **sacrificial metal**. This means even if the coating is damaged, the **zinc** will corrode first, protecting the **iron** underneath.
 
• The most common industrial method is **hot-dip galvanizing**, where the metal parts are submerged in a bath of **molten zinc** at temperatures typically around **450°C (842°F)**.
 
• This technique provides two types of protection: a **physical barrier** that prevents moisture and oxygen from reaching the iron, and **cathodic protection**, which is an **electrochemical** defense mechanism.
 
• **Zinc** is highly effective for this purpose because it bonds **metallurgically** to the **iron** or **steel**, creating a series of **zinc-iron alloy** layers that are extremely durable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Chemistry of Protection:** When **zinc** is exposed to the atmosphere, it reacts with **oxygen** to form **zinc oxide (ZnO)**. questions.question: What does the velocity-time graph look like for an object moving with uniform velocity?

options.text: A straight line parallel to the time axis

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A straight line parallel to the time axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform velocity** refers to a state of motion where an object covers equal **displacements** in equal intervals of **time**, regardless of how small these intervals are. In this state, both the **magnitude** (speed) and the **direction** of the object remain **constant**.
 
• In a **velocity-time (v-t) graph**, the **velocity** of the object is typically represented on the **vertical y-axis**, while the **time** elapsed is represented on the **horizontal x-axis**.
 
• Since the velocity is **constant** during uniform motion, the value on the y-axis does not change as the value on the x-axis (time) increases. This results in a **horizontal straight line** that is **parallel to the time axis**.
 
• The **slope** of a velocity-time graph indicates the **acceleration** of the moving object. For an object with uniform velocity, the **acceleration is zero** (since there is no change in velocity), which mathematically corresponds to a **slope of zero**.
 
• This graphical representation is a primary tool in **kinematics** to distinguish between **uniform** and **non-uniform motion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Displacement from v-t Graph**: The **area enclosed** under the velocity-time curve and the time axis provides the **total displacement** of the object over a given **time interval**. For uniform velocity, this area is simply a **rectangle** (Velocity × Time).
 
• **Uniform Acceleration**: When the velocity-time graph is a **straight line sloping upwards** starting from the **origin** or any other point, it represents **uniform acceleration**. This means the velocity increases by **equal amounts** in equal intervals of **time**.
 
• **Uniform Retardation**: A **straight line sloping downwards** on a v-t graph indicates **uniform retardation** (or negative acceleration), where the velocity of the object decreases at a **constant rate** until it potentially comes to **rest**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Acceleration**: If the velocity-time graph is a **curved line** (rising gradually or otherwise), it indicates **non-uniform acceleration**. In this case, the **rate of change of velocity** is not constant over time.
 
• **Position-Time Graph**: It is important to note that for **uniform velocity**, the **position-time (s-t) graph** would be a **straight line sloping upwards** at a constant angle, indicating that displacement is **directly proportional** to time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Instantaneous Velocity**: In the case of **uniform motion**, the **instantaneous velocity** at any given **second** is exactly equal to the **average velocity** over any duration.
 
• **Zero Velocity**: If the object is at **rest**, its velocity is **zero**, and the velocity-time graph will be a straight line coinciding with the **time axis (x-axis)** itself.
 
• **Direction**: If the straight line parallel to the time axis is in the **negative quadrant** (below the x-axis), it indicates the object is moving with a constant velocity in the **opposite direction**.
 
• **Units**: Standard **SI units** for plotting these graphs are **meters per second (m/s)** for the y-axis and **seconds (s)** for the x-axis.

• **Holozoic nutrition** is a type of **heterotrophic nutrition** that involves the **ingestion** of liquid or solid organic material, followed by its **internal digestion**, absorption, and assimilation to provide energy.

• **Saprophytic organisms** (saprobes) derive their nutrition from **dead and decaying organic matter** like fallen leaves, dead animals, or rotting bread.
 
• Unlike holozoic organisms, they perform **extracellular digestion** by secreting enzymes outside their body to break down complex matter and then absorbing the **liquefied nutrients**. Common examples include **Fungi** (like **Mushrooms** and **Yeast**) and certain **Bacteria**.
 
 
 
• **Parasitic Nutrition:**
 
 
• In this mode, an organism (the **parasite**) lives on or inside another living organism (the **host**) and obtains its food **at the expense of the host** without killing it immediately.
 
• They can be **Ectoparasites** (living outside, like **Leeches** and **Lice**) or **Endoparasites** (living inside, like **Tapeworms** and **Ascaris**). A famous plant parasite is **Cuscuta** (Amarbel).

• **Key Biological Features:**
 
 
• **Heterotrophs**: Both holozoic, parasitic, and saprophytic organisms fall under the broad category of **Heterotrophs** because they cannot produce their own food and depend on other sources for **organic carbon**.
 
• **Digestive System**: Holozoic nutrition usually requires a **specialized digestive tract** or a **food vacuole** (as in **unicellular organisms** like Paramecium) to process the ingested material.

• **Holozoic**: Internal digestion of **solid/liquid** food.
 
• **Saprophytic**: External digestion of **dead matter**.
 
• **Parasitic**: Absorption of nutrients from a **living host**.
 
• **Autotrophic**: Synthesis of food using **Solar energy** or **Chemical energy**.

questions.question: A sealed packet has a mass of 500 g and a volume of 350 cm³ . Given the density of water is 1 g cm⁻³ , will the packet float or sink in water, and why?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sink, because its density is greater than water's density.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Density** is defined as the **mass** of an object per unit **volume**. It determines whether an object will float or sink in a given fluid.
 
• In the given problem, the **mass** of the sealed packet is **500 g** and its **volume** is **350 cm3**.
 
• The formula for calculating density is **Density = Mass / Volume**. By substituting the values, we get: **500 g / 350 cm3** = **1.428 g/cm3** (approximately **1.43 g/cm3**).
 
• The **density of water** is a standard value of **1 g/cm3** (or **1000 kg/m3**).
 
• An object **sinks** in a fluid if its density is **higher** than the density of the fluid. Since **1.43 g/cm3** is greater than **1 g/cm3**, the packet will definitely sink in water. ***Hence, the statement regarding sinking due to higher density is correct.***
 
• The **buoyant force** (upthrust) acting on the packet is equal to the weight of the water displaced by the volume of the packet (**350 cm3**), which weighs **350 g**. Since the actual weight of the packet (**500 g**) is more than the upthrust, it cannot float.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Archimedes' Principle**: This principle states that when a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an **upward force** (buoyancy) that is equal to the **weight of the fluid displaced** by it.
 
• **Conditions for Floating and Sinking**:
 
 
• If **Density of Object Density of Fluid**: The object will **sink**.
 
 
 
• **Relative Density (Specific Gravity)**: It is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of water. If the **relative density** is greater than **1**, the substance will sink in water. For this packet, the relative density is **1.43**.
 
• **Mass vs. Weight**: **Mass** is a measure of the amount of matter in an object (measured in **grams** or **kilograms**), whereas **weight** is the force exerted by gravity on that mass (measured in **Newtons**). In floatation problems, we often use mass and density for simplicity in **CGS units** (g/cm3).
 
• **Applications**: This concept is crucial in designing **ships**, **submarines**, and **hot air balloons**. A large iron ship floats because its **average density** (including the air inside) is less than that of water, even though iron itself is much denser.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Standard Values**: The density of **pure water** is highest at **4 degrees Celsius**, being exactly **1.00 g/cm3**. **Saltwater** has a higher density (approx **1.025 g/cm3**), which is why it is easier for humans to float in the ocean than in a freshwater pool.
 
• **Numerical Fact**: To find the mass of the water displaced by the packet, we multiply its volume (**350 cm3**) by the density of water (**1 g/cm3**), resulting in **350 g** of water displaced.
 
• **Misconception**: An object does not sink just because it has a "high mass" or a "low volume"; it sinks because of the **relationship (ratio)** between mass and volume. A **1 kg** block of wood will float, while a **10 g** iron nail will sink.

• **Structure of Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are **double-membrane-bound** organelles. The **outer membrane** is smooth and porous, while the **inner membrane** is deeply folded into structures called **cristae**.
 
• The **cristae** increase the **surface area** available for chemical reactions, specifically the **Electron Transport Chain (ETC)**, which is vital for **ATP production**.
 
• The internal compartment filled with fluid is known as the **matrix**, which contains enzymes for the **Krebs cycle**.
 
 
 
• **Semi-Autonomous Nature:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are considered **semi-autonomous** because they possess their own **circular DNA** and **70S ribosomes**, allowing them to synthesize some of their own proteins.
 
• They reproduce independently within the cell through a process similar to bacterial division called **binary fission**.
 
 
 
• **Functions:**
 
 
• The primary function is **aerobic respiration**, earning them the title **"Powerhouse of the cell"**.
 
• They also play roles in **calcium storage**, **apoptosis** (programmed cell death), and **heat production** (thermogenesis).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery and Naming:** Mitochondria were first observed by **Albert von Kolliker** in **1850** as granules in muscle cells. **Richard Altmann** described them as "bioblasts" in **1890**, and the term "mitochondria" was officially coined by **Carl Benda** in **1898**.
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:** This biological theory suggests that mitochondria originated from **free-living prokaryotes** (specifically proteobacteria) that entered into a symbiotic relationship inside a host **eukaryotic cell** billions of years ago.
 
• **Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA):** Unlike nuclear DNA, **mtDNA** is inherited almost exclusively from the **mother** in humans, making it a crucial tool for tracing **ancestry** and studying **evolutionary biology**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements explains why insectivorous plants evolved to trap insects?

options.text: To compete with herbivores for space
To take cellulose from plant tissues
To supplement nitrogen and other nutrients
To survive in habitats with low sunlight

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To supplement nitrogen and other nutrients**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insectivorous plants**, also known as **carnivorous plants**, have evolved to trap and digest insects because they typically grow in **nutrient-poor soils**, particularly those lacking in **nitrogen**.
 
• Nitrogen is a vital component for the synthesis of **proteins, chlorophyll, and nucleic acids** in plants. In environments like **bogs, marshes, and swamps**, the soil is often **acidic and waterlogged**, which prevents the decomposition of organic matter and makes nitrogen unavailable to plants.
 
• While these plants possess **chlorophyll** and are capable of **photosynthesis** to produce carbohydrates, they rely on animal prey to acquire essential minerals like **nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium** that the soil cannot provide. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• These plants do not trap insects to compete with **herbivores for space**; rather, they occupy **ecological niches** where other plant species struggle to survive due to mineral deficiencies. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• They do not consume insects to take **cellulose**, as cellulose is a structural component of **plant cell walls**, not animal tissues; furthermore, plants synthesize their own cellulose. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Insectivorous plants often require **bright sunlight** for photosynthesis and are not specifically adapted to survive in **low sunlight** habitats through insect consumption. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Common Examples of Insectivorous Plants:**
 
 
• **Venus Flytrap (Dionaea muscipula):** Native to the **subtropical wetlands** of the **United States (North and South Carolina)**. It uses a **snap trap** mechanism triggered by sensitive **trigger hairs**.
 
• **Pitcher Plant (Nepenthes & Sarracenia):** Uses a **pitfall trap**. The leaves are modified into a **jug-like structure** filled with **digestive liquor**. **Nepenthes khasiana** is a species found in **Meghalaya, India**.
 
• **Sundew (Drosera):** These plants use **flypaper traps**. Their leaves are covered in **tentacles** that secrete a sticky, glistening substance called **mucilage** to ensnare prey.
 
• **Bladderwort (Utricularia):** These are **aquatic** or terrestrial plants that use **suction traps** (bladders) to capture small organisms like **water fleas** in **freshwater** habitats.
 
 
 
• **Digestive Mechanism:**
 
 
• Once an insect is trapped, the plant secretes **digestive enzymes** such as **proteases, esterases, and acid phosphatases**.
 
• These enzymes break down the animal's **proteins and soft tissues** into simple **nitrogenous compounds** (amino acids) and **minerals**, which are then absorbed by the leaf surfaces.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Partial Heterotrophs:** Insectivorous plants are described as **partial heterotrophs** because they are **autotrophic** (produce their own food via photosynthesis) but **heterotrophic** for specific mineral requirements.
 
• **Habitat Features:** They are most commonly found in **perennially wet** areas with **low pH (acidic)**. High acidity slows down the **nitrifying bacteria** that normally convert organic nitrogen into forms plants can use.
 
• **Conservation:** Many insectivorous plants are **threatened or endangered** due to **habitat loss** and **illegal collection**. For instance, the **Pitcher Plant** in India is protected under the **Wildlife Protection Act**.
</ul

options.text: They are produced during sexual reproduction.

Processes like **crossing over** during **meiosis** and the **independent assortment** of chromosomes ensure that offspring have a unique genetic makeup. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

questions.question: Which of the following metals does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid under normal conditions?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper** is a metal that does **not react** with **dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl)** under normal conditions. This is because **Copper** is placed below **hydrogen** in the **reactivity series** of metals.
 
• In a reaction between a metal and a dilute acid, the metal must displace **hydrogen** from the acid to form a **metal salt** and release **hydrogen gas**. Since **Copper** is less reactive than **hydrogen**, it cannot lose electrons to the **hydrogen ions (H+)** present in the acid. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• **Zinc** is more reactive than hydrogen and sits higher in the **activity series**. When it comes into contact with **dilute HCl**, it reacts steadily to form **Zinc Chloride (ZnCl2)** and evolves **hydrogen gas**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Aluminium** is a highly reactive metal. Although it often has a protective **Aluminium Oxide layer**, once that layer is bypassed, it reacts vigorously with **dilute HCl** to produce **Aluminium Chloride (AlCl3)** and **hydrogen gas**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Iron** is also positioned above hydrogen in the **reactivity series**. It reacts slowly with **dilute hydrochloric acid** at **room temperature** to form **Ferrous Chloride (FeCl2)** and **hydrogen gas**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series**: This is a series of metals arranged in the **decreasing order** of their **reactivity**. Metals like **Potassium (K)**, **Sodium (Na)**, and **Calcium (Ca)** are at the top, while **Gold (Au)** and **Platinum (Pt)** are at the bottom. Metals above **hydrogen** can displace it from **dilute acids**, while those below it (**Copper, Mercury, Silver, Gold**) cannot.
 
• **Reaction with Nitric Acid**: While **Copper** does not react with **dilute HCl**, it can react with **Nitric Acid (HNO3)**. However, this is not a simple **displacement reaction**; because **Nitric Acid** is a strong **oxidizing agent**, it oxidizes the metal, and instead of **hydrogen gas**, oxides of **nitrogen** (like NO or NO2) are evolved.
 
• **Aqua Regia**: Noble metals like **Gold** and **Platinum** do not react even with concentrated **HCl** or **Nitric acid** individually. They only dissolve in **Aqua Regia**, which is a freshly prepared mixture of **concentrated Hydrochloric acid** and **concentrated Nitric acid** in a **3:1 ratio**.
 
• **Physical Properties of Copper**: It is a **reddish-brown** transition metal with the atomic number **29**. It is widely used in **electrical wiring** due to its high **electrical conductivity** and in **alloying** to create **Brass** and **Bronze**.
 
• **Hydrogen Gas Test**: When metals above hydrogen react with **dilute HCl**, the evolved **hydrogen gas** can be tested using a **burning splinter**, which extinguishes with a characteristic **"pop" sound**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aluminium's Passivity**: Sometimes **Aluminium** appears to not react immediately with acids. This is due to a thin, tough layer of **Aluminium Oxide (Al2O3)** on its surface. Once the acid dissolves this layer, the **exothermic reaction** proceeds rapidly.
 
• **Chemical Equations**:
 
 
• **Zinc**: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2
 
• **Iron**: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2
 
• **Aluminium**: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl3 + 3H2
 
• **Copper**: Cu + HCl → **No Reaction**
 
 
 
• **Standard Reduction Potential**: From an **electrochemical** perspective, metals with a **negative reduction potential** (like Zinc and Iron) can displace hydrogen, whereas metals with a **positive reduction potential** (like Copper, +0.34V) cannot.
</ul

questions.question: What happens when a solid is heated continuously?

options.text: It expands and turns into a gas
It melts and may later evaporate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It melts and may later evaporate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **solid** is heated, the **thermal energy** is absorbed by its particles, which increases their **kinetic energy**. As the particles gain energy, they vibrate more vigorously around their fixed positions.
 
• As heating continues, the substance reaches its **Melting Point**. At this specific temperature, the energy supplied is used to break the **intermolecular forces of attraction** that hold the particles in a rigid lattice structure.
 
• The process of a solid changing into a liquid is known as **Fusion** or **Melting**. During this phase change, the temperature remains constant even though heat is still being added; this heat is known as the **Latent Heat of Fusion**.
 
• Once the entire solid has turned into a **liquid**, further heating will cause the temperature of the liquid to rise. The particles in the liquid move faster and more freely.
 
• Eventually, the liquid reaches its **Boiling Point**, where the particles gain enough energy to completely overcome the remaining attractive forces and transition into the **gaseous state** through **evaporation** or **boiling**. ***Hence, the correct progression is that the solid melts and may later evaporate.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **States of Matter:**
 
 
• **Solid**: Particles are packed closely together in a regular pattern with very **low kinetic energy** and **high intermolecular attraction**. They have a **fixed shape** and **fixed volume**.
 
• **Liquid**: Particles are close together but can slide past each other. They have a **fixed volume** but **no fixed shape**, taking the shape of the container.
 
• **Gas**: Particles are far apart and move randomly at **high speeds**. They have **no fixed shape** and **no fixed volume**, expanding to fill any space available.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Expansion:** Most solids undergo **expansion** when heated before they reach their melting point. This occurs because the increased vibration of particles increases the **average distance** between them, causing the overall volume of the solid to increase slightly.
 
• **Phase Transitions:**
 
 
• **Sublimation**: A rare process where a solid turns directly into a gas without passing through the liquid phase. Examples include **Dry Ice (Solid Carbon Dioxide)**, **Naphthalene**, and **Camphor**.
 
• **Vaporization**: The transition from liquid to gas. This includes **Evaporation** (which occurs at the surface below the boiling point) and **Boiling** (which occurs throughout the bulk of the liquid at a specific temperature).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Latent Heat:** This is the "hidden" heat absorbed or released by a substance during a change in its **physical state** (phase) that occurs without changing its temperature.
 
 
• **Latent Heat of Fusion**: For water, this value is approximately **334 Joules per gram** at **0 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization**: For water, this value is approximately **2260 Joules per gram** at **100 degrees Celsius**.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:** The strength of these forces determines the **Melting Point** and **Boiling Point** of a substance. Substances with **stronger bonds** (like ionic solids) require more energy (higher temperatures) to melt compared to those with **weaker bonds** (like molecular solids).
 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:** This theory explains that **temperature** is a direct measurement of the **average kinetic energy** of the particles in a substance. Therefore, continuous heating is synonymous with increasing the energy of the constituent particles.
</ul

questions.question: The Supreme Court declared in October 2025 that the principle of public trust extends to artificial lakes this ruling affirmed the directive of which of the following High Court benches?

options.text: Jaipur Bench of the Rajasthan High Court
Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court
Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court
Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, in a landmark judgment delivered in **October 2025**, expanded the legal horizon of environmental protection by ruling that the **Public Trust Doctrine** applies equally to **artificial lakes** and man-made water bodies.
 
• This specific ruling affirmed a previous directive issued by the **Nagpur Bench** of the **Bombay High Court**, which had emphasized that the state acts as a trustee for all water resources regardless of their origin. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court.***
 
• The court observed that the ecological significance of a water body does not depend on whether it was formed naturally or constructed by human intervention, as both serve vital **environmental functions** like groundwater recharge and climate regulation.
 
• The **Public Trust Doctrine** mandates that the state holds certain resources in trust for the general public and cannot permit their conversion for private ownership or commercial exploitation that harms the public interest.
 
• This judgment reinforces the interpretation of **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India**, which encompasses the right to a wholesome environment as part of the **Right to Life**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Public Trust Doctrine:** 
 
 
• Originating from **Roman Law**, it was first integrated into Indian law by the **Supreme Court** in the case of **M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997)**.
 
• It establishes that resources like **air, sea, waters, and forests** have such a great importance to the people as a whole that it would be wholly unjustified to make them a subject of private ownership.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Framework:** 
 
 
• **Article 48A**: This **Directive Principle of State Policy** directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
 
• **Article 51A(g)**: It is a **Fundamental Duty** of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment, including **lakes**, rivers, and wildlife.
 
 
 
• **Bombay High Court:** 
 
 
• Established on **August 14, 1862**, it is one of the oldest and most prestigious High Courts in India.
 
• It has jurisdiction over the states of **Maharashtra** and **Goa**, and the Union Territory of **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**.
 
• The **Nagpur Bench** is one of its permanent benches, along with **Aurangabad** and **Panaji**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Artificial Lakes:** 
 
 
• In many urban areas, **artificial lakes** are the primary sources of **micro-climate maintenance** and biodiversity hubs.
 
• Protecting them under the Public Trust Doctrine prevents land mafias and developers from reclaiming lake beds for **real estate** projects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The ruling is expected to impact various **smart city projects** and urban development plans across **India** where man-made reservoirs were previously considered exempt from strict environmental non-alienation rules.
 
• The **October 2025** verdict clarifies that once a territory is designated as a water body in **revenue records**, its status cannot be changed easily, even if it is currently dry or was originally man-made.
 
• This legal precedent provides a powerful tool for **environmental activists** to challenge the encroachment of historic tanks and reservoirs constructed during various eras of Indian history.

• **Strategic Significance:**
 
 
• The development of **VLSRSAM** is a significant step toward **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) in the defense sector, as it is designed and developed indigenously by **DRDO** laboratories like **RCI Hyderabad** and **DRDL**.
 
• It is specifically optimized to counter **supersonic sea-skimming missiles**, which fly very close to the water surface to avoid radar detection, making **low-altitude engagement** a critical requirement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with other options:**
 
 
• **Underwater deployment:** This capability is associated with **Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missiles (SLBMs)** or torpedoes, not the **VLSRSAM**, which is surface-launched.
 
• **Mid-course ballistic target destruction:** This is the domain of **Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD)** systems like the **Prithvi Air Defence (PAD)** or **Advanced Air Defence (AAD)**, rather than short-range tactical missiles.
 
• **Long-range high-altitude interception:** Systems like the **S-400** or **Long Range Surface-to-Air Missile (LRSAM/Barak-8)** handle long-range threats, whereas **VLSRSAM** is specialized for **short-range** protection.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Prof. Syed Wajih Ahmad Naqvi, an outstanding Biogeochemical Oceanographer with national and international recognition, received the 2024 Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar in which of the following categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vigyan Shri (VS) Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prof. Syed Wajih Ahmad Naqvi**, a distinguished **Biogeochemical Oceanographer**, was honored with the **Vigyan Shri (VS) Award** in **2024**.
 
• He received this prestigious recognition in the domain of **Earth Science** for his pioneering contributions to marine science and biogeochemistry. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP)** is the highest national award in the field of science, technology, and innovation in **India**, established to recognize outstanding contributions by scientists and technologists.
 
• The **Vigyan Shri (VS) Award** specifically recognizes **distinguished contributions** to any field of science and technology.
 
• Prof. Naqvi has significantly enhanced the understanding of **oceanic nitrogen cycles**, particularly in the **Arabian Sea** and the **Indian Ocean**, gaining both national and international acclaim.
 
• He previously served as the **Director** of the **CSIR-National Institute of Oceanography (NIO)**, based in **Goa**, where he led numerous research expeditions and institutional developments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP) Categories**:
 
 
• **Vigyan Ratna (VR)**: Awarded for **lifetime achievements** and contributions in any field of science and technology.
 
• **Vigyan Shri (VS)**: Awarded for **distinguished contributions** in any field of science and technology.
 
• **Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar (VY-SSB)**: Designed to recognize young scientists up to the **age of 45 years** who have made exceptional contributions.
 
• **Vigyan Team (VT)**: Awarded to a **team** consisting of **three or more** scientists/researchers for collaborative work.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility and Domains**:
 
 
• The awards are given in **13 specific domains**, including **Physics, Chemistry, Biological Sciences, Mathematics & Computer Science, Earth Science, Medicine, Engineering Sciences, Agricultural Science, Environmental Science, Technology & Innovation, Atomic Energy, Space Science and Technology**, and **Others**.
 
• The selection is made by the **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar Committee (RVPC)**, which is headed by the **Principal Scientific Adviser** to the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 2024**:
 
 
• The year **2024** marked the **inaugural edition** of the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar, consolidating various previous science awards under one umbrella.
 
• A total of **33 awards** were announced in the first edition across the four categories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The awards were presented by the **President of India**, **Droupadi Murmu**, at a ceremony held at **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
 
• The announcement of the awards coincided with **National Space Day**, celebrated on **August 23**, to commemorate the success of the **Chandrayaan-3** mission.
 
• **Prof. Naqvi's** research is crucial for understanding **marine hypoxia** (low oxygen zones) and how climate change affects **ocean chemistry** and **marine life**.
 
• The award comprises a **Sanad (Certificate)** and a **Medal**, emphasizing the recipient's dedication to advancing the scientific landscape of **India**.
</ul
